collection_metadata.locality: Pitchandikulam Forest, Auroville, Tamil Nadu, India

stem_bark.text: The bark of Cassia fistula is ash-grey-coloured, smooth and warty. The  bark flakes off in crusty scales on old trees.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Cassia fistula is ash-grey-coloured, smooth and warty. The bark flakes off in crusty scales on old trees.

seed.text: The seeds of Cassia fistula are in separated compartments with walls about 2-3 mm apart. The seeds are brown-coloured, flattened, ovate, 8-9 mm long and 7-8 mm wide.
seed.text_html:
The seeds of Cassia fistula are in separated compartments with walls about 2-3 mm apart.
The seeds are brown-coloured, flattened, ovate, 8-9 mm long and 7-8 mm wide.

fruit.text: The fruit of Cassia fistula is a very long and cylindrical pod . It is smooth, mucronate, up to 50 cm long and about 2 cm across. These glossy, pendulous and indehiscent pods turn from green to black at maturity.
fruit.text_html:
The fruit of Cassia fistula is a very long and cylindrical pod .
It is smooth, mucronate, up to 50 cm long and about 2 cm across.
These glossy, pendulous and indehiscent pods turn from green to black at maturity.

flower.text: The flowers of Cassia fistula are grouped in axillary and many-flowered racemes. These inflorescences are large (up to 15-40 cm long), pendulous and bright yellow. The peduncle is 4-6 cm long. The flowers are 5-merous. The calyx is composed of a cup-shaped, green and pubescent calyx-tube and 5 yellow-greenish calyx-lobes . These calyx-lobes are obovate-orbicular, 7-8 mm long and 6-7 mm wide. The corolla is composed of 5 bright yellow, obovate, short-clawed and unequal petals . They are glabrous, veined and 2.5-3 cm long and 1.5-2 cm wide with a 3 mm long claw. The androecium is composed of 10 stamens , 3 of them are as long as the style and 7 are shorter. The stamens have erected filaments and basifixed anthers . The style is light green, slender and curved. It is 2.5-3 cm long with a simple stigma at the tip.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Cassia fistula are grouped in axillary and many-flowered racemes. These inflorescences are large (up to 15-40 cm long), pendulous and bright yellow.
The peduncle is 4-6 cm long.
The flowers are 5-merous.
The calyx is composed of a cup-shaped, green and pubescent calyx-tube and 5 yellow-greenish calyx-lobes. These calyx-lobes are obovate-orbicular, 7-8 mm long and 6-7 mm wide.
The corolla is composed of 5 bright yellow, obovate, short-clawed and unequal petals. They are glabrous, veined and 2.5-3 cm long and 1.5-2 cm wide with a 3 mm long claw.
The androecium is composed of 10 stamens, 3 of them are as long as the style and 7 are shorter. The stamens have erected filaments and basifixed anthers.
The style is light green, slender and curved. It is 2.5-3 cm long with a simple stigma at the tip.

leaf.text: The leaves of Cassia fistula grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The leaf is compound, paripinnate with a 4-6 cm long petiole and 4 to 8 pairs of large leaflets. The leaflets are bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaflets are coriaceous and glabrous on both sides. The leaflets have a 5-6 mm long petiolule . The leaflet of Cassia fistula is 8-12 cm long and 4-5 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate, the apex is acute, the base is cuneate and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Cassia fistula is a medium-sized and deciduous tree growing up to 10-12 m high with a spreading and irregular crown.

reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :
    Cassia fistula is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).
  • Mode of pollination :
    Cassia fistula is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.
  • Seed dispersal :
    Zoochory : The seeds of Cassia fistula are extensively dispersed by monkey, jackals, pigs and others mammals which break the pods to eat the pulp and thus scatter the seeds. (Sahni, 1998, The Book of Indian Trees)

    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.

phenology.text: ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )
phenology.text_html:
• Flowering season : From May to November.
  • Fruiting season : From November to March.
  • Seeding season : From November to March.
  • Leaves falling : During the hot season.

    • (This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains)

others.text: Cassia fistula is widely planted as an ornamental tree . It is an extremely showy tree in bloom.
others.text_html: Cassia fistula is widely planted as an ornamental tree. It is an extremely showy tree in bloom.

handicrafts.text: The wood of Cassia fistula is durable and takes a good and lasting polish. It is used for house and bridge posts, wheels, cart building, agricultural implements, tool handles, rice pounder, turnery and furniture. The bark is a useful tanning material, known as sumari . Source : Dastur, 2006, Useful Plants of India and Pakistan

reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :
    Cassia fistula is a fast growing species able to flourish in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining.
    The species prefers full sun but can withstand moderate shade.
    Cassia fistula is propagated by seeds.
  • Seed treatments :
    The seeds of Cassia fistula germinate readily without treatment but scarification and soaking accelerate the germination.
